name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
summary: Seoul’s grandest Joseon palace, backed by Bugaksan — and free during Chuseok 24–27 Sep 2026 with guard ceremonies.
description: Built in 1395, Gyeongbokgung is the largest of Seoul’s five royal palaces, with the throne hall Geunjeongjeon and the lotus-pond pavilion Gyeonghoeru set against the mountains. The courtyards are wide and flat, so the walking is easy for parents. The National Folk Museum sits inside the grounds. During Chuseok 2026 admission is free and the royal guard ceremonies run daily.
highlights: Gyeonghoeru pavilion on its lotus pond
Hyangwonjeong pavilion in the north garden
tips: Chuseok 24–27 Sep: free entry; guard-changing 10:00 & 14:00, guard-duty ritual 11:00 & 13:00, patrol 15:00 — no booking needed.
Closed Tuesdays — 29 Sep is a closed day. Last entry is one hour before closing.
Anyone wearing hanbok gets in free on any day; rental shops cluster around Gyeongbokgung Station exit 4.
Go at 09:00 opening before tour buses; exit via the north gate toward Samcheong-dong for cafés.

name: Changdeokgung Palace & Secret Garden
summary: UNESCO palace that follows the hills, with Huwon, the Joseon kings’ Secret Garden, on a guided tour.
description: Changdeokgung was the Joseon kings’ favourite residence and is the palace most in harmony with its landscape, which earned it UNESCO status. The main grounds are free during Chuseok, but the Secret Garden (Huwon) — ponds, pavilions and a centuries-old juniper — is seen only on a timed, paid tour. The garden route is hilly and takes about 90 minutes.
highlights: Buyongji pond and Juhamnu pavilion in the Secret Garden
Autumn colour in the Huwon woods
tips: The Secret Garden is EXCLUDED from free Chuseok entry — book the tour online ahead; slots sell out on holidays.
Closed Mondays — 28 Sep is closed.
The garden walk climbs; parents who dislike stairs can enjoy the flat main palace and skip Huwon.
Walk straight on into Changgyeonggung next door via the connecting gate.

name: Jongmyo Shrine
summary: UNESCO royal ancestral shrine with one of the longest wooden halls in Asia — no booking needed 24–27 Sep.
description: Jongmyo holds the spirit tablets of Joseon kings and queens. tips: 24–27 Sep: free, no reservation — a rare chance to wander at your own pace.

name: Bukchon Hanok Village
summary: Hillside lanes of tiled-roof hanok homes between two palaces — a lived-in residential area with visiting hours.
description: Bukchon is the largest cluster of traditional hanok houses in Seoul, climbing the slope between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung. description: Yeouido Hangang Park is the city’s liveliest stretch of riverbank, with wide lawns, bike rentals, food trucks and convenience stores selling instant ramyeon. Tripadvisor ranks it #10 in Seoul; reviewers say everyone comes at sundown. The Hangang Bus water bus stops at the Yeouido pier.
highlights: Sunset picnic with delivered fried chicken
Han River ramyeon from a riverside convenience store
tips: Order chimaek to the park’s delivery zones — delivery apps list the pickup points.
Crowded on holiday evenings; weekday late afternoons are best.
Yeouinaru Station (Line 5) exit 2/3 opens right onto the park.

tripadvisor.rank: #10 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: A great place for a family walk or run.
Everyone comes at sundown — crowded but a chilled spot for snacks and views.
Naver visitors highlight views, photos and good walking paths.

name: Ttukseom Hangang Park
summary: East-side river park with the caterpillar-shaped Jabeolle pavilion, festivals and drone shows.
description: Ttukseom sits right at Jayang (Ttukseom Hangang Park) Station, whose platforms overlook the river. The Jabeolle — a tube-shaped pavilion from the station into the park — houses exhibitions and views. It is the stage for many Han River festivals: the 2026 Seoul Autumn Festa opened here on 18 Sep.
tips: Station exits lead straight into the park — minimal walking for parents.
Check Seoul Autumn Festa listings for performances here during the trip.
Tripadvisor reviewers warn it is vast; agree a meeting point.

name: Nodeul Island
summary: A mid-river island under Hangang Bridge with lawns, a live-music hall and a newly opened waterside space.
description: Nodeul Island sits in the middle of the Han under Hangang Bridge, reached on foot or by bus. Its lawn faces a classic sunset over the river and the 63 Building, with a small music hall, bookshop and food trucks (Sep–Oct 2026). The "Nodeul Global Art Island" redevelopment has opened a new waterside culture space, while lower-level works continue.
highlights: Sunset over the Han and Yeouido
Pop-up library and live music programmes
tips: Indoor spaces close 25 Sep only; outdoor areas stay open 24 h.
Parts of the lower island are under construction — follow signs.
Buses stop on the bridge; from Nodeul Station (Line 9) it is a ~10 min walk.

reviews.text: Nodeul Island’s notices list September programs — pop-up library, picnic day and live music — and food trucks through October 2026.
Naver posts focus on sunset views of the river and relaxed lawn picnics.

hours.note: Outdoor areas 24 h; indoor facilities have set hours (changed 2–11 Oct 2026).

chuseok.note: Indoor facilities closed on Chuseok day 25 Sep 2026; outdoor spaces open 24 h regardless (official notice).

name: Seonyudo Park
summary: A former water-treatment plant on a Han River island turned into an award-winning garden of concrete ruins and plants.
description: Seonyudo Park reuses the tanks, pillars and pipes of an old filtration plant as terraced gardens, aquatic plant pools and shaded colonnades, reached by the arched Rainbow Bridge. It is a landmark of Korean landscape architecture but far less visited than Yeouido. Naver reviewers praise the views and walking paths.
highlights: Aquatic plant ponds in old tanks
tips: Hidden gem: design lovers’ favourite that most tourists skip.
Opens 06:00 and closes at night — check exit times.
Seonyudo Station (Line 9 — same line as home) exit 2, 10 min walk.

reviews.text: Naver keywords: great view, photogenic, lots to see, well-made paths.
Seoul parks agency describes the island as a small peak once celebrated by poets for its scenery.

name: Seoul Forest
summary: A big leafy park next to Seongsu with deer, ginkgo avenues, ponds and a butterfly garden.
description: Seoul Forest covers a former racecourse by the Han with woods, lawns, ponds, a deer enclosure and an insect and butterfly garden (May–Oct). Tripadvisor reviewers love its space for picnics and cycling in the middle of the city. It pairs perfectly with the Seongsu café streets next door.
tips: Seoul Forest Station (Suin-Bundang) exit 3 is at the park edge.
Grab coffee in Seongsu then picnic on the lawns.
Butterfly garden last entry 16:30.

tripadvisor.rank: #13 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: Nature in the middle of the city, spacious enough to sit, play or cycle.
The ginkgo forest was lovely as the trees turned yellow.

hours.note: Park 24 h; ecological forest opens 05:30; butterfly garden last entry 16:30

name: Seokchon Lake
summary: A 2.5 km lakeside loop at the foot of Lotte World Tower — the prettiest walk before or after Seoul Sky.
description: Seokchon Lake’s two basins are ringed by a flat, tree-lined promenade with Lotte World Tower and Lotte World’s castle reflected in the water. It is where locals jog and stroll in the evening. Tripadvisor reviewers praise its cleanliness and calm.
highlights: Lotte World Tower reflection at dusk
Lotte World castle across the water
tips: Do Seoul Sky at sunset, then walk the lake as the tower lights up.
Easy option: the west lake loop is ~20 min and flat; skip the full 40-min circuit.

tripadvisor.rank: #97 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: Great location — lake, greenery, cleanliness, tranquillity.
One of the most recommended cherry-blossom spots in Seoul.

summary: Korea’s flagship arts complex, a short walk from home: galleries, opera house, concert hall and a plaza.
description: Seoul Arts Center gathers the Opera House (its roof shaped like a gat hat), Concert Hall, Hangaram Art Museum, Hangaram Design Museum and Calligraphy Museum below Umyeonsan. Even without a ticket the plazas and gardens are pleasant. It is the closest major cultural venue to home — about a 10-minute walk.
highlights: Opera House and Concert Hall performances
tips: Walk from home (~10 min) or Nambu Bus Terminal Station exit 5.
Check sac.or.kr for concerts on your nights — good-value seats appear last-minute.
Hangaram Design Museum opened a Hispanic Society collection show from 22 Sep 2026.

A worthwhile exhibition visit with a huge, superb collection.

name: Seorae Village & Montmartre Park
summary: Seoul’s French quarter by home: a flat street of French bakeries and bistros, with Montmartre Park’s lawns at the end.
description: Seorae Village grew around the French school, and Seorae-ro still has French bakeries, bistros and wine bars. Uphill, Montmartre Park and the connected Seoripul forest trails form a large wooded hill park with free-roaming rabbits and views over Seocho — Tripadvisor reviewers say you forget you are in the city. Locals love it; tourists rarely come.
tips: Easy option: 5-min taxi to Seorae-ro and stroll the flat bakery street; Montmartre Park’s entrance lawn is a short walk from its end.
The forest trails beyond the park climb — skip them if legs are tired.
Naver reviewers note it is uncrowded.

tripadvisor.rank: #212 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: A massive park — you can walk for miles in the forest and forget you are in the city.
Lots of tame rabbits in the park that do not run away when you approach.

hours.note: Park open 24 h; bakeries from about 08:00

name: National Library of Korea
summary: Korea’s national library near home — calm exhibition halls, a sleek digital library and a hillside café.
description: The National Library sits beside Seorae Village, a short walk from home. Beyond the stacks it has free exhibitions on Korean books and printing, and a digital library with screens and study pods. It is quiet, air-conditioned and almost unknown to tourists — a good rainy-hour stop combined with Seorae.
highlights: Free exhibitions on Korean books and printing
Café with stairs overlooking the hill
tips: Hidden gem: free and minutes from home.
Visitors need a free pass at the entrance with ID for reading rooms; exhibitions are open.
Closed on some Mondays and major holidays — check nl.go.kr before going on 25 Sep.

reviews.text: A modest number of Naver visitor reviews, mostly from students and locals enjoying the quiet study spaces.
Wikimedia Korea documented a partnership ceremony at the library, reflecting its role as the national archive.

summary: Tall-tree forest park in south Seocho with a memorial to independence hero Yun Bong-gil — lovely in autumn.

Combine with the Yangjaecheon stream walk and café street.

summary: Leafy stream paths under old trees with a café street at Yeongdong 1-gyo — Gangnam locals’ evening stroll.

tips: Easy option: taxi 10 min to Yeongdong 1-gyo, stroll 15–20 min along the flat path, finish at a café.
Evenings are lovely and cooler under the trees.

name: Chuseok Free Palace & Royal Shrine Opening
summary: Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Deoksugung, Changgyeonggung and Jongmyo are free 24–27 Sep 2026, with guard ceremonies.
description: For Chuseok 2026 the Cultural Heritage Administration opens the four main palaces, Jongmyo and the Joseon royal tombs free of charge from 24 to 27 September. Jongmyo needs no reservation, visitors in hanbok enter without ticketing, and Gyeongbokgung stages its royal guard ceremonies daily. Paid special programs — the Changdeokgung Secret Garden, moonlight tours and night openings — are excluded.
highlights: Free entry to four palaces and Jongmyo
tips: Regular closures still apply: Changdeokgung/Changgyeonggung/Deoksugung closed Mon 28; Gyeongbokgung & Jongmyo closed Tue 29.
Go early: holiday afternoons get very crowded.
Secret Garden still needs a paid tour booking.

reviews.text: Asia Economy reports the four palaces, Jongmyo and royal tombs are free for four days, with Jongmyo open without reservation.
Herald Business notes hanbok wearers enter without ticketing and paid programs such as the Secret Garden are excluded.

name: The Art Spot — Chuseok Performances at the National Museum
summary: Free gugak, fusion and street-performance shows in the NMK’s open-air yard, 24, 26 and 27 Sep at 13:00 & 15:00.
description: The National Museum of Korea and the Korea Traditional Performing Arts Foundation stage free shows in the museum’s outdoor Yeollin Madang during Chuseok. tips: Combine with the museum (free) — arrive 12:00, see the 13:00 show, then galleries.
Outdoor: may move or change in rain.

name: Namsan Moonlight Madang (Chuseok Festival)
summary: Tightrope walking, Arirang, quilting and hanbok try-ons at Namsangol Hanok Village, 25–27 Sep, 10:00–20:00.
description: Seoul’s Namsangol Hanok Village marks Chuseok with "Namsan Moonlight Madang": traditional tightrope (jultagi), Arirang and gugak performances, seven hands-on traditional experiences, a master-led nubi quilting craft, hanbok dressing and braided-hair styling. tips: Some experiences are paid; performances are free.

name: Seoul Outdoor Library — Chuseok Late Nights
summary: Beanbags, books and lights at Seoul Plaza, Gwanghwamun and Cheonggyecheon — open until 22:00, 25–27 Sep.
description: Seoul’s popular Outdoor Library sets out bookshelves, beanbags and parasols in three downtown spots. Over Chuseok 2026 all three — "Reading Seoul Plaza", "Gwanghwamun Book Yard" and "Reading Clear Stream" on Cheonggyecheon — run from 16:00 to 22:00. It is a relaxed, free evening stop after the palaces.
highlights: Gwanghwamun Book Yard beside the Sejong statue
tips: Free and walk-in; English picture books are limited — come for the atmosphere.
Perfect tired-family pause between Gyeongbokgung and dinner.

name: Seoul Autumn Festa 2026
summary: Umbrella festival linking some 200 dance, gugak, theatre and outdoor shows across Seoul, 18 Sep – 29 Nov 2026.
description: Seoul Autumn Festa ties together hundreds of performances and festivals across the city for 73 days, opening with "Seoul, Dance on the Han River" at Ttukseom on 18 Sep. During the trip it offers dance, gugak and theatre programmes, many outdoors and free. Check the festival listings for shows on your free evenings.
highlights: Dance, gugak and theatre across the city
tips: Browse the programme for events near Banpo or Seoul Arts Center to keep evenings close to home.
The Seoul Hangang International Dance Festival follows at Banpo’s Yebit Island stage on 1–3 Oct.

reviews.text: News1 reports the Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture runs the 73-day festival from 18 Sep to 29 Nov.
Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon attended the Ttukseom opening, where the festival was described as linking pure performing-arts festivals.

chuseok.note: Festival spans the holiday; individual shows vary — check listings.

name: Yoo Youngkuk: The Mountain Is Within Me
summary: Free, largest-ever retrospective of Korea’s abstract painter of mountains at SeMA Seosomun, to 25 Oct 2026.
description: Marking the 110th anniversary of his birth, the Seoul Museum of Art presents about 170 works and archives by Yoo Youngkuk — including 115 oil paintings — tracing six decades of bold colour-field mountains. Admission is free and no reservation is needed. The museum is open through Chuseok.
highlights: Archive of a Korean abstraction pioneer
tips: Fridays open to 21:00 ("Seoul Culture Night"); closed Mondays.
Five minutes from Deoksugung — pair them in one evening.

reviews.text: Kyunghyang’s Chuseok exhibition guide calls it the biggest retrospective of Yoo’s lifelong focus on mountains, free 24–27 Sep.
Listings give the run as 19 May – 25 Oct 2026, Tue–Fri 10:00–20:00 and weekends 10:00–19:00, Fridays to 21:00.

chuseok.note: Seoul city museums open and free 24–27 Sep 2026.

name: MMCA Free Chuseok Days & Do Ho Suh Retrospective
summary: All MMCA branches free 24–27 Sep; the Seoul branch’s Do Ho Suh retrospective is 2026’s hottest show (closed 25 Sep).
description: MMCA opens its Seoul, Gwacheon, Deoksugung and Cheongju branches free of charge for Chuseok. The Seoul branch’s large Do Ho Suh retrospective — three decades of fabric architecture, thread drawings and recent projects about home and identity — draws queues daily. Also showing: Korea Artist Prize 2026 and "This Is (Not) Conceptual Art". Deoksugung branch shows Lee Dai-won inside the palace.
highlights: Do Ho Suh’s translucent fabric houses
tips: Free but ticketed — book online; if sold out, on-site timed tickets are first-come.
Seoul branch closed 25 Sep; Deoksugung and Gwacheon branches open all four days.
Instagram #2026추석맞이국현미 (23–27 Sep) enters a Do Ho Suh soap draw.

reviews.text: Kyunghyang says the Do Ho Suh show has people queuing daily and on-site slot tickets are issued first-come when online sells out.
